# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book is intended for people entering railway signalling from a general engineering background and for practising technicians who need a concise reference to the systems they maintain.

It is designed to support, rather than replace, company training, controlled standards, maintenance specifications, local instructions or competence arrangements.

## How to use this book

The early chapters are intended to be read in order. Equipment-specific chapters follow a consistent structure so they can also be used as practical reference material.

::: {.callout-important title="Principle"}
Safety or engineering principles that explain why a signalling system is designed or operated in a particular way.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="In practice"}
How the principle normally appears in real equipment, drawings or maintenance work.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Fault finding"}
A diagnostic observation, reasoning method or worked fault-finding example.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="Trivia"}
A local note, or trivia.
:::


## Scope

The first edition concentrates on equipment and systems encountered within the author's section. The underlying principles are explained broadly enough to remain useful when other equipment is encountered later.

## Safety and authority

This book is educational material. Where it differs from current controlled company documentation, the controlled documentation takes precedence.
